Day 14 & 15 · 2 & 3 Nov

Riemann sum and definite integrals

The schedule also lists a review of Calculus midterm 1 for these two classes. That paper, with worked answers, is under Past midterms on the Calculus midterm 1 page.

  • The idea: to find the area under y=f(x)y=f(x)y=f(x) from x=ax=ax=a to x=bx=bx=b, cut it into nnn thin strips, treat each strip as a rectangle, add up the rectangles, and let n→∞n\to\inftyn→∞.
  • Strip width and sample points: every strip has the same width Δx=b−an\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}Δx=nb−a​ Strip kkk (for k=1,2,…,nk=1,2,\dots,nk=1,2,…,n) gets its height f(xk)f(x_k)f(xk​) at one point xkx_kxk​ of the strip: right end: xk=a+k Δxleft end: xk=a+(k−1) Δxmidpoint: xk=a+(k−12)Δx\begin{aligned}\text{right end: }x_k&=a+k\,\Delta x\\[2pt]\text{left end: }x_k&=a+(k-1)\,\Delta x\\[2pt]\text{midpoint: }x_k&=a+\left(k-\tfrac{1}{2}\right)\Delta x\end{aligned}right end: xk​left end: xk​midpoint: xk​​=a+kΔx=a+(k−1)Δx=a+(k−21​)Δx​ The slides write NNN for the number of strips: it is the same as nnn here.
  • Riemann sum and definite integral: Sn=∑k=1nf(xk) Δx∫abf(x) dx=lim⁡n→∞Sn\begin{gathered}S_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}f(x_k)\,\Delta x\\[6pt]\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\lim_{n\to\infty}S_n\end{gathered}Sn​=k=1∑n​f(xk​)Δx∫ab​f(x)dx=n→∞lim​Sn​​ Here aaa is the lower limit and bbb the upper limit. Left ends, right ends and midpoints all give the same limit.
  • Partial sums: ∑k=1n1=n∑k=1nk=n(n+1)2∑k=1nk2=n(n+1)(2n+1)6∑k=1nk3=n2(n+1)24\begin{aligned}\sum_{k=1}^{n}1&=n\\[2pt]\sum_{k=1}^{n}k&=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\\[2pt]\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^2&=\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}\\[2pt]\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^3&=\frac{n^2(n+1)^2}{4}\end{aligned}k=1∑n​1k=1∑n​kk=1∑n​k2k=1∑n​k3​=n=2n(n+1)​=6n(n+1)(2n+1)​=4n2(n+1)2​​ A constant comes out of the sum: ∑c ak=c∑ak.\sum c\,a_k=c\sum a_k.∑cak​=c∑ak​.
  • Five steps: find Δx\Delta xΔx, write xkx_kxk​, work out f(xk)f(x_k)f(xk​), add up with the partial sums (constants out first), then let n→∞n\to\inftyn→∞. When a≠0a\ne0a=0, expand f(a+kΔx)f(a+k\Delta x)f(a+kΔx) and split it into separate sums.
  • The class example, x2x^2x2 from 000 to LLL (right ends, xk=kLnx_k=\frac{kL}{n}xk​=nkL​): Sn=L3n3∑k=1nk2=L36⋅(n+1)(2n+1)n2→L36⋅2=L33\begin{aligned}S_n&=\frac{L^3}{n^3}\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^2\\[4pt]&=\frac{L^3}{6}\cdot\frac{(n+1)(2n+1)}{n^2}\\[4pt]&\to\frac{L^3}{6}\cdot2=\frac{L^3}{3}\end{aligned}Sn​​=n3L3​k=1∑n​k2=6L3​⋅n2(n+1)(2n+1)​→6L3​⋅2=3L3​​
  • Signed area: where f<0f<0f<0, the terms f(xk)Δxf(x_k)\Delta xf(xk​)Δx are negative, so the integral is the area above the xxx-axis minus the area below it. For the actual area, split at the zeros of fff and add the parts as positive numbers.
  • The class example, x2+x−2x^2+x-2x2+x−2 on [0,2][0,2][0,2]: f=(x+2)(x−1)f=(x+2)(x-1)f=(x+2)(x−1) is negative on [0,1)[0,1)[0,1) and positive on (1,2](1,2](1,2]. With right ends, Sn=23+6n+43n2→23S_n=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{6}{n}+\frac{4}{3n^2}\to\frac{2}{3}Sn​=32​+n6​+3n24​→32​ The integral 23\frac{2}{3}32​ is 116\frac{11}{6}611​ above the axis minus 76\frac{7}{6}67​ below it, but the area of the region is 116+76=3.\frac{11}{6}+\frac{7}{6}=3.611​+67​=3. Practice works it out step by step.
  • The shortcut: with a primitive FFF of fff (that is, F′=fF'=fF′=f), the integral is F(b)−F(a)F(b)-F(a)F(b)−F(a). The next lesson uses it for every integral; the Riemann sum stays the definition.

Watch out

  • Δx=b−an.\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}.Δx=nb−a​. It is 1n\frac{1}{n}n1​ only when the interval has length 111.
  • When a≠0a\ne0a=0, keep the aaa in xk=a+kΔxx_k=a+k\Delta xxk​=a+kΔx, and expand before you split the sum.
  • A constant is added nnn times: ∑k=1n3=3n,\sum_{k=1}^{n}3=3n,∑k=1n​3=3n, not 333. In the class example the −2-2−2 gives −4-4−4 in SnS_nSn​, not −4n-\frac{4}{n}−n4​.
  • "Compute the Riemann sum" asks for SnS_nSn​ as a formula in nnn. Write it out before you take the limit, and don't replace it with F(b)−F(a)F(b)-F(a)F(b)−F(a).
  • An integral is a signed area: ∫02(x−1) dx=0,\mathord{\int_0^2(x-1)\,dx}=0,∫02​(x−1)dx=0, yet the region between the line and the axis has area 111.

Day 16 & 17 · 5 & 6 Nov · Quiz 06

Primitive functions (indefinite integrals)

  • The limit of the Riemann sum: on an interval [a,b][a,b][a,b] with NNN strips and right ends, the general form is SN=∑k=1Nf ⁣(a+k(b−a)N)b−aNS_N=\sum_{k=1}^{N}f\!\left(a+\frac{k(b-a)}{N}\right)\frac{b-a}{N}SN​=k=1∑N​f(a+Nk(b−a)​)Nb−a​ and ∫abf(x) dx=lim⁡N→∞SN.\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\lim_{N\to\infty}S_N.∫ab​f(x)dx=limN→∞​SN​. On [0,1][0,1][0,1] it is SN=1N∑k=1Nf ⁣(kN)S_N=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N}f\!\left(\frac{k}{N}\right)SN​=N1​∑k=1N​f(Nk​): put x=kNx=\frac{k}{N}x=Nk​ into fff, then use the partial sums.
  • Exchange of initial and final points: running from bbb back to aaa makes every Δx\Delta xΔx negative, so the integral changes sign. An interval of width 000 gives 000: ∫baf(x) dx=−∫abf(x) dx∫aaf(x) dx=0\begin{aligned}\int_b^a f(x)\,dx&=-\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\\[2pt]\int_a^a f(x)\,dx&=0\end{aligned}∫ba​f(x)dx∫aa​f(x)dx​=−∫ab​f(x)dx=0​ Joining intervals adds the integrals, ∫abf dx+∫bcf dx=∫acf dx,\int_a^b f\,dx+\int_b^c f\,dx=\int_a^c f\,dx,∫ab​fdx+∫bc​fdx=∫ac​fdx, and the integral of a sum splits into the integrals of its terms, with constants coming out.
  • Primitive function: FFF is a primitive function (an antiderivative) of fff when F′(x)=f(x)F'(x)=f(x)F′(x)=f(x). For example x33\frac{x^3}{3}3x3​ is a primitive of x2x^2x2, because (x33)′=x2.\left(\frac{x^3}{3}\right)'=x^2.(3x3​)′=x2.
  • Ambiguity in the primitive function: if FFF is a primitive of fff, so is F+CF+CF+C for every constant CCC, because a constant has derivative 000. On an interval, any two primitives of the same fff differ only by a constant, so one condition, such as F(1)=4F(1)=4F(1)=4, picks one of them.
  • Indefinite integral: the whole family of primitives is written ∫f(x) dx=F(x)+C\int f(x)\,dx=F(x)+C∫f(x)dx=F(x)+C where CCC is the integration constant. Like the derivative, it splits over sums and lets constants out: ∫(αf+βg) dx=α∫f dx+β∫g dx\int(\alpha f+\beta g)\,dx=\alpha\int f\,dx+\beta\int g\,dx∫(αf+βg)dx=α∫fdx+β∫gdx
  • Definite integral from a primitive: any primitive FFF of fff gives ∫abf(x) dx=[F(x)]ab=F(b)−F(a)\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\Big[F(x)\Big]_a^b=F(b)-F(a)∫ab​f(x)dx=[F(x)]ab​=F(b)−F(a) The CCC cancels, so leave it out here. This replaces the limit of SNS_NSN​ whenever a primitive is known.
  • Fundamental primitive functions: each one is a derivative rule read backwards (b>0b>0b>0, b≠1b\ne1b=1): ∫xn dx=xn+1n+1+C(n≠−1)∫1x dx=ln⁡∣x∣+C∫ex dx=ex+C∫bx dx=bxln⁡b+C∫sin⁡x dx=−cos⁡x+C∫cos⁡x dx=sin⁡x+C∫1cos⁡2x dx=tan⁡x+C∫11+x2 dx=arctan⁡x+C\begin{aligned}\int x^n\,dx&=\frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}+C\quad(n\ne-1)\\[2pt]\int\frac{1}{x}\,dx&=\ln|x|+C\\[2pt]\int e^x\,dx&=e^x+C\\[2pt]\int b^x\,dx&=\frac{b^x}{\ln b}+C\\[2pt]\int\sin x\,dx&=-\cos x+C\\[2pt]\int\cos x\,dx&=\sin x+C\\[2pt]\int\frac{1}{\cos^2x}\,dx&=\tan x+C\\[2pt]\int\frac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx&=\arctan x+C\end{aligned}∫xndx∫x1​dx∫exdx∫bxdx∫sinxdx∫cosxdx∫cos2x1​dx∫1+x21​dx​=n+1xn+1​+C(n=−1)=ln∣x∣+C=ex+C=lnbbx​+C=−cosx+C=sinx+C=tanx+C=arctanx+C​ Check any of them by differentiating the right-hand side.
  • A number inside: divide by it. The chain rule multiplies by aaa, so the primitive divides by aaa (a≠0a\ne0a=0): ∫eax dx=1aeax+C∫bax dx=baxaln⁡b+C∫sin⁡ax dx=−1acos⁡ax+C∫cos⁡ax dx=1asin⁡ax+C\begin{aligned}\int e^{ax}\,dx&=\frac{1}{a}e^{ax}+C\\[2pt]\int b^{ax}\,dx&=\frac{b^{ax}}{a\ln b}+C\\[2pt]\int\sin ax\,dx&=-\frac{1}{a}\cos ax+C\\[2pt]\int\cos ax\,dx&=\frac{1}{a}\sin ax+C\end{aligned}∫eaxdx∫baxdx∫sinaxdx∫cosaxdx​=a1​eax+C=alnbbax​+C=−a1​cosax+C=a1​sinax+C​
  • Logarithms: ∫1x dx=ln⁡∣x∣+C\int\frac{1}{x}\,dx=\ln|x|+C∫x1​dx=ln∣x∣+C covers the one power the power rule can't (n=−1n=-1n=−1), and the absolute value makes it work for x<0x<0x<0 too. With ax+bax+bax+b inside, ∫1ax+b dx=1aln⁡∣ax+b∣+C\int\frac{1}{ax+b}\,dx=\frac{1}{a}\ln|ax+b|+C∫ax+b1​dx=a1​ln∣ax+b∣+C
  • Rewrite first: turn roots and fractions into powers, x=x1/2\sqrt{x}=x^{1/2}x​=x1/2 and 1x2=x−2,\frac{1}{x^2}=x^{-2},x21​=x−2, and a power in the denominator into a negative exponent: 13x=3−x,\frac{1}{3^x}=3^{-x},3x1​=3−x, so ∫13x dx=−3−xln⁡3+C.\int\frac{1}{3^x}\,dx=-\frac{3^{-x}}{\ln3}+C.∫3x1​dx=−ln33−x​+C. Split a fraction over its denominator, or factor it, before you integrate.
  • arctan: arctan⁡x\arctan xarctanx, also written tan⁡−1x\tan^{-1}xtan−1x, is the angle between −π2-\frac{\pi}{2}−2π​ and π2\frac{\pi}{2}2π​ whose tan is xxx. The −1-1−1 means the inverse function, not 1tan⁡x\frac{1}{\tan x}tanx1​. From the exact values, arctan⁡0=0,arctan⁡13=π6arctan⁡1=π4,arctan⁡3=π3\begin{gathered}\arctan0=0,\quad\arctan\tfrac{1}{\sqrt3}=\tfrac{\pi}{6}\\[2pt]\arctan1=\tfrac{\pi}{4},\quad\arctan\sqrt3=\tfrac{\pi}{3}\end{gathered}arctan0=0,arctan3​1​=6π​arctan1=4π​,arctan3​=3π​​ and arctan⁡(−x)=−arctan⁡x.\arctan(-x)=-\arctan x.arctan(−x)=−arctanx.
  • Area with a primitive: find the zeros of fff inside [a,b][a,b][a,b], work out each piece with FFF, and add the pieces as positive numbers. Without the split, the parts below the axis are subtracted.

Watch out

  • The minus sign belongs to sine: ∫sin⁡x dx=−cos⁡x+C,\int\sin x\,dx=-\cos x+C,∫sinxdx=−cosx+C, because (cos⁡x)′=−sin⁡x.(\cos x)'=-\sin x.(cosx)′=−sinx.
  • Divide by the number inside, never multiply: ∫cos⁡3x dx=13sin⁡3x+C\int\cos3x\,dx=\frac{1}{3}\sin3x+C∫cos3xdx=31​sin3x+C and ∫e−x dx=−e−x+C.\int e^{-x}\,dx=-e^{-x}+C.∫e−xdx=−e−x+C.
  • ∫1x dx=ln⁡∣x∣+C,\int\frac{1}{x}\,dx=\ln|x|+C,∫x1​dx=ln∣x∣+C, since the power rule would divide by 000. And ∫12x+1 dx=12ln⁡∣2x+1∣+C,\int\frac{1}{2x+1}\,dx=\frac{1}{2}\ln|2x+1|+C,∫2x+11​dx=21​ln∣2x+1∣+C, not ln⁡∣2x+1∣+C\ln|2x+1|+Cln∣2x+1∣+C.
  • With the variable in the exponent, ∫2x dx=2xln⁡2+C,\int2^x\,dx=\frac{2^x}{\ln2}+C,∫2xdx=ln22x​+C, not 2x+1x+1.\frac{2^{x+1}}{x+1}.x+12x+1​. And ∫13x dx\int\frac{1}{3^x}\,dx∫3x1​dx is not ln⁡∣3x∣\ln|3^x|ln∣3x∣: rewrite it as 3−x3^{-x}3−x first.
  • tan⁡−1x\tan^{-1}xtan−1x is arctan⁡x\arctan xarctanx, an angle: tan⁡−11=π4,\tan^{-1}1=\frac{\pi}{4},tan−11=4π​, while 1tan⁡1\frac{1}{\tan1}tan11​ is a different number.
  • In F(b)−F(a)F(b)-F(a)F(b)−F(a), work out F(a)F(a)F(a) on its own line, then subtract all of it: [−cos⁡x]0π=−cos⁡π−(−cos⁡0)=2.\mathord{\Big[-\cos x\Big]_0^{\pi}}=-\cos\pi-(-\cos0)=2.[−cosx]0π​=−cosπ−(−cos0)=2. With a negative limit, −(−2)=+2-(-2)=+2−(−2)=+2.
  • An area question needs the zeros of fff first: ∫−11x dx=0,\mathord{\int_{-1}^{1}x\,dx}=0,∫−11​xdx=0, but the area between y=xy=xy=x and the axis on [−1,1][-1,1][−1,1] is 111.
  • Check every primitive by differentiating it back to fff.

Exam-day habits

  • Write Δx\Delta xΔx and xkx_kxk​ first, then f(xk)f(x_k)f(xk​). Most mistakes happen in these two lines.
  • Take constants out of every sum before you use a partial-sum formula, and remember ∑k=1nc=cn.\sum_{k=1}^{n}c=cn.∑k=1n​c=cn.
  • Give SnS_nSn​ as a formula in nnn, then take the limit.
  • Check a primitive by differentiating it: (−cos⁡x)′=sin⁡x.(-\cos x)'=\sin x.(−cosx)′=sinx.
  • In a definite integral, leave out the CCC, and work out F(b)F(b)F(b) and F(a)F(a)F(a) on separate lines before you subtract.
  • When fff changes sign, find its zeros first: the integral and the area of the region are different answers.
  • Keep answers exact: 163\frac{16}{3}316​, π4\frac{\pi}{4}4π​ or e2−12\frac{e^2-1}{2}2e2−1​, not decimals.
